newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Zuma says not in conflict with drug firms.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Zuma says not in conflict with drug firms.

text.p: South African health minister Nkosazana Zuma said on Friday that she was not in conflict with the drugs industry, despite having recently been challenged in court by SmithKline Beecham Plc.
"The department of health is not at loggerheads with the pharmaceutical industry," Zuma said in a statement.
Zuma's relationship with the industry has, however, been rocky as in October she backed down from a SmithKline legal challenge over proposed reforms.
The plans had wanted to make prescribing generic drugs mandatory and limit the dispensing of medicines. New proposals are now being drawn up.
The statement was issued as Zuma opened a 2.5 million rand joint-venture betweeen the health department, South African Druggists Ltd's Pharmacare unit, and the medical arm of the South African army.
The project is to provide facilities for primary healthcare and emergency training for nurses and orderlies. It will train 120 people a year.
"Where there is a need we come together... I challenge other companies to follow this excellent example and to turn words and promises into actions," Zuma said.
